title: SCIM + SAML attribute normalization and deprovision hedging playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Customers using SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning send a variety of attribute formats (emails with mixed case, external IDs that vary by IdP, group displayName vs. uniqueName, and nested group structures). We have observed multiple incidents where deprovisioning requests from IdPs caused accidental user removals due to mismatched attributes, and retries caused duplicate remediation attempts that created audit noise. This ticket defines an engineering playbook to: 1) normalize SAML->SCIM attribute mappings deterministically; 2) introduce a deprovision hedging/quarantine window with idempotent safe-guards and backoff retries; 3) ensure RBAC v2 admin rules and audit logs capture both intent and outcome for every SCIM deprovision event.

Scope: attribute normalization (primaryEmail, externalId, nameId), mapping rules for group identifiers, dedupe rules for group merges, idempotency keys for provisioning/deprovisioning requests, retry strategy (exponential with jitter + adaptive circuit-breaker), quarantine/hedge period behavior, UI/Console flags for admin approval, and audit trail enrichment (actor, original SAML assertion, normalized keys, retry attempts). Excludes: deep federation syncing (handled in separate project).

Why now: Recent customer incident (INC-2025-019) showed a tenant lost developer access after a noisy IdP re-sync. This is priority due to potential enterprise SLA/contract risk.
acceptance_criteria: SCIM pipeline implements deterministic attribute normalization rules for common SAML attributes (email lowercasing with unicode normalization, mapping nameId->externalId fallback, canonical group identifier selection)
Deprovision flow uses an idempotency token stored with event metadata so repeated retries do not cause repeated removals or duplicate remediation signals
Quarantine window configurable per-tenant (default 72 hours) where deprovision events are surfaced to console and sent to admins for manual approval before hard deletion
Automatic safe-path rollback for mistaken deprovisions (reprovision from last known good snapshot) available and documented in runbook
Retry policy implemented with exponential backoff + jitter, max attempts configurable, and a soft circuit-breaker that pauses retries on >N failures per minute
